text: Sun conjunct Mars fuses who you are with what you do. Will and identity run on the same circuit, so there is no gap in you between wanting something and moving toward it. This shows up as heat other people can feel: energy, nerve, a readiness to compete that does not switch off just because the stakes are small. You take life personally, in the specific sense that every task feels like a test of you rather than a thing to be done. That makes you formidable, and it makes you tired. The gifts are plain. You have courage of the ordinary, usable kind: you say the hard thing, make the first move, and defend people who are being pushed around. Vitality tends to run strong, and you feel best when your body is spent honestly, through work, sport, or effort with a visible result. Idleness does not rest you; it backs up in you as restlessness or a short fuse. In your working life you are the one who breaks stalemates. Where a group circles a decision, you act, and the group quietly relies on that even while complaining about your bluntness. The costs come from the same fusion. Because action and self are one thing to you, being blocked can feel like being erased, and small obstacles sometimes draw a response sized for large ones. Impatience is the daily tax: with slow processes, with cautious people, with your own learning curve. Temper flares fast, and though it burns out fast too, others may not recover on your schedule. You can also start more than you can honorably finish, since the beginning is where the fire lives. In love you bring directness and real passion, and you respect a partner who pushes back. What needs watching is the habit of turning the relationship into one more arena, where a disagreement must be won rather than understood. Warmth and rivalry can blur for you, and the people closest to you should not have to fight for the tenderness underneath. The growth built into this aspect is aim. Your force was never the problem; unaimed force is. Timing, patience with middles, choosing which fights are actually yours: each of these turns raw heat into power that lasts longer than an afternoon. When you pick a few efforts worth years and let the rest go unfought, the drive that once scattered itself across every provocation starts producing a life that looks the way you feel: strong, direct, and unmistakably yours.

A sextile between the Sun and Mars gives you energy on call. It does not run your life the way a stronger contact would; it waits like a trained muscle and answers when asked. When you decide something matters, drive shows up: you push through resistance, speak plainly under pressure, and keep working after others have folded, all without much inner drama. Assertion sits at a healthy volume in you. You can say no, ask for what you want, and hold a line without turning the moment into a battle, which is rarer than it sounds. People read you as confident but not combative, and that combination opens doors. Colleagues hand you the difficult conversations, and friends borrow your nerve when their own runs short. Physical energy responds the same way: your body rewards use, regular effort steadies your mood and sharpens your focus, and long idle stretches dull you more than they rest you. The one catch with a sextile is that it is an offer, not a compulsion. Nothing forces you to use this. Left alone, it becomes a pleasant sense that you could be decisive, could compete, could push, someday, about something. The talent stays real but theoretical. What draws it out is a stake: a goal with your name on it, a deadline that will not move, a person worth defending. Give it one of those and the whole apparatus wakes at once, often to your own surprise. In love you tend toward honest, low-games affection. You show interest plainly instead of maneuvering, and you handle conflict better than most, since anger neither frightens you nor floods you. To you it is information about where the line is, and once the line is clear you can be warm again within the hour. Work that mixes initiative with cooperation suits you, because you can lead without needing to dominate and follow without feeling erased. Growth here is mostly a matter of appetite. The aspect will match whatever you ask of it, and asking too little is the only real way to waste it. Each time you volunteer for something slightly beyond your current reach, the ease you were given compounds into actual strength. Years of that turn a knack for handling pressure into a record of things built on purpose, which is the quiet best case for this aspect: not a loud life, but a mover's life, chosen one manageable risk at a time.

Sun square Mars wires a permanent argument into you between what you intend and how you act. The energy is enormous, but it arrives at an angle: you push hardest at the wrong moment, say the sharp thing a beat before thinking, or pour effort into proving a point nobody was contesting. Life with this aspect can feel like driving a powerful car whose steering pulls. Irritation lives close to your surface. Delays, incompetence, and being told what to do can take you from calm to hot in seconds, and the anger often lands on people who were not its cause. Authority is a recurring flashpoint. Something in you meets instruction as challenge, and the early years may collect friction with bosses, teachers, and anyone holding a clipboard. It is worth saying plainly that none of this is a defect of character. The square is friction between two strong drives, your sense of self and your force of action, and friction is also how engines work. People who stay with this aspect tend to out-build and outlast their smoother peers, precisely because nothing was easy and they kept going anyway. Struggle taught them pacing; the lucky ones never had to learn it. In close relationships the pattern shows as heat: quick quarrels, strong desire, and a tendency to test partners by pushing. The people who last with you learn that your flare is not contempt. You learn, more slowly, that some things said in thirty hot seconds take thirty days to repair, and that a temper is a cost you can budget once you admit you have one. The long work of this square is separating drive from reaction. Rage is the unrefined form; endurance, nerve, and honest directness are the refined ones, and the refining happens through use, not suppression. Hard exercise, demanding projects, and causes with real opposition give the force somewhere to go and something to become. Deprived of a worthy outlet, it will manufacture unworthy ones, which is why your quietest seasons are sometimes your most quarrelsome. In middle life, most people carrying this square notice a strange reversal. The trait that made them difficult when young has made them durable, colleagues start calling the bluntness clarity, and the fights they no longer need to have become the clearest measure of how strong they actually got.

With the Sun trine Mars, confidence is your resting state. Will and energy cooperate in you so smoothly that you may not recognize it as a trait at all; it just feels like being awake. You decide, you act, and the acting does not cost you the inner negotiation it costs most people. Fear of confrontation, paralysis before risk, the long stall between wanting and doing: these are famous human problems you mostly know secondhand. The ease shows everywhere. At work you take initiative without drama and defend your position without heat, which reads as natural authority. Physically you tend to be resilient, with energy that renews on ordinary sleep and good spirits that hold up under load. In love you are direct about desire and steady in conflict, since disagreement does not feel like danger to you. People relax around your confidence because it is not aggressive; it does not need anyone smaller in order to feel tall. The weakness of a trine is the flip side of its gift: nothing about it demands growth. Because assertion came free, you may never train it, and untested ease has a ceiling. You can coast, choosing paths of pleasant momentum over ones that would ask more of you, and arrive at midlife strong but unstretched. There is also a blind spot with other people. What is effortless for you is genuinely hard for most, and breezy advice to just speak up or just go for it can land as carelessness on someone whose nerve costs them dearly. Patience with slower, more fearful people is a skill this aspect does not include; you have to add it yourself. The invitation here is voluntary difficulty. Your confidence deepens only against real resistance: the ambitious project, the honest competition, the goal far enough away that ease alone will not reach it. Sought on purpose, difficulty turns a happy temperament into earned strength, and the difference shows the first time life applies pressure you did not choose. Once you have struggled at something real, your natural courage picks up the one thing it lacked, which is sympathy. From there you become more than a fortunate person. You become the one who lends nerve to others, steadies rooms simply by being unafraid in them, and makes bravery look, for an hour at a time, contagious.

Sun opposite Mars puts your force on the far side of the table. The drive is fully yours, but you tend to meet it face to face, in other people: the rival who keeps appearing, the pushy colleague, the partner whose temper somehow always goes first. Life arranges itself as a series of encounters with someone else's will, and the recurring question is how much of that heat you carried into the room yourself. Oppositions work through relationship, and this one makes you a specialist in contest. You may notice that you are sharpest with an opponent, that your best work arrives under challenge, and that pure solitude leaves your engine idling. Nothing is wrong with that; some people are built to strike sparks off others. The trouble starts when the pattern runs unowned. If you think of yourself as reasonable and mild, your unclaimed aggression does not vanish. It gets delegated. You pick fierce friends, provoke quietly and react loudly, or swing between long patience and sudden eruptions that feel, to you, like the other person's fault. The signature of this aspect is the phrase they made me angry, spoken sincerely. Close relationships carry the most voltage. You are drawn to strong-willed people, partly because you are looking for your own strength in them, and the same partner can feel thrilling in year one and combative in year three. The relationships that work are the ones where conflict is legal: where both of you can push, disagree openly, and trust the bond to hold. Peace bought with swallowed anger does not hold; it leaks, usually sideways, usually at home. Work has its own version of the theme. You do well in negotiation, advocacy, competitive fields, anywhere the job is to meet an opposing force squarely, and you struggle most in settings that require pretending everyone agrees. The maturing of this opposition is repatriation. Every time you catch the heat rising and say plainly that this is my anger, I want this, I am competing right now, you take a piece of your force back from the far side of the table. Owned, it is tremendous: courage, stamina, and a gift for honest confrontation that others find clarifying rather than frightening. The opponents never entirely stop coming, but they change meaning. They stop being ambushes and become sparring partners, and you start winning the only fight that was ever really yours.

Sun conjunct Jupiter blends who you are with the urge to grow, and the result is a kind of built-in yes. You experience yourself as someone meant for more: more experience, more understanding, more room. This is not vanity so much as metabolism. Hope comes easily to you. Where others see a closed door, you assume a hinge, and the assumption is right often enough to look like luck. The warmth is real and it travels. You are generous by reflex, with money, praise, second chances, and time, and people leave your company feeling larger than they arrived. Doors open partly because of this: benefactors, mentors, and lucky breaks find optimists, since optimists are still standing where the breaks land. You think in wholes rather than parts, which suits you for teaching, leading, persuading, or any work where someone has to hold the big picture and make others believe in it. The bill for all this expansiveness is proportion. Everything in you trends toward more, including error. You overpromise, because at the moment of promising you sincerely feel that large. You overspend, overeat, overcommit the calendar, and take on projects sized for the self you are becoming rather than the one currently available. Confidence can inflate past its collateral, and then others experience you as grandiose, careless with details, or blind to the fine print of your own life. Disappointment hits you strangely hard, since your inner weather assumes fair skies, and a season of shrunken circumstances can feel like a personal injustice rather than an ordinary turn. In love you are openhanded and encouraging, a genuine builder of the other person, though you may promise a future faster than you can construct it, and a partner who keeps the receipts can start to seem like the enemy of joy instead of its accountant. Your growth, fittingly, is not about becoming smaller. It is about delivery. Vision matters exactly as much as its execution, and every time you finish what you announced, close the loop, and let results speak, your natural faith stops being a mood and becomes a reputation. The luck was always partly you; it deepens when you give it structure. Then the bigness stops needing an audience, and you become what this conjunction promises at its best: a person whose presence widens other people's sense of what is possible.

The sextile between your Sun and Jupiter is a door that opens when you knock, and only then. It carries the classic gifts of this pair: optimism, decent judgment, a knack for being liked, and a life that seems to offer chances at useful moments. But it offers rather than insists. The openings, introductions, and well-timed strokes of fortune arrive at the edge of your life, and whether they become anything depends on whether you step toward them. Your temperament helps. You carry a baseline good faith about the future that steadies you and reassures others; you assume problems have solutions and start looking rather than lamenting. This makes you good company in a crisis and a natural moderate in disputes, able to find the reasonable middle without much strain. Teachers, mentors, and helpful elders appear across your life more often than chance would predict, drawn by the fact that you actually listen. Growth suits you in steps: the course finally taken, the trip finally booked, the offer followed up within the week. Fortune here compounds like interest rather than striking like lightning, and the compounding is easy to miss until you look back across a decade. What the aspect will not do is compel you. Its ease can read as mildness, a pleasant sense that things are fine as they are, and years can pass in comfortable underuse. The chances keep knocking softly, and a busy or timid season can miss them without ever noticing something was missed. There is no crisis in this aspect to force your hand, which is exactly why your hand has to move on its own. In love and friendship you bring tolerance and humor, and you tend to grow through your relationships, picking up worldviews, places, and possibilities from the people you let close. Choosing companions who are themselves growing matters more for you than for most, since you expand by association and contract the same way. The art of this sextile is responsiveness. Notice the door and knock back: say yes to the stretch assignment, follow the curiosity while it is warm, write to the person who offered help and meant it. Each accepted invitation widens the next one. Over the years, what began as a quiet aptitude for luck becomes something sturdier, a practiced habit of turning openings into a broader and more generous life.

Sun square Jupiter gives you an appetite one size larger than your plate. The urge to grow rubs against your sense of who you are, and the friction usually shows as overshoot: you promise more than the week can hold, spend tomorrow's money on today's enthusiasm, and take on the project that needed two of you. Restlessness hums underneath everything. Whatever you have, some part of you is already discounting it and scanning for more. It helps to understand what this is not. It is not greed, and calling it mere excess misses the engine. Something in you genuinely refuses a small life, and that refusal is the best thing about you when it is yoked to real work. People with this square found ventures, cross oceans, and talk institutions into ideas too big for committees, precisely because their reach exceeds their grasp on schedule. The costs are just as real. Overconfidence writes checks: the missed detail, the deadline treated as a suggestion, the sure thing that needed a fallback and did not have one. Self-importance can creep in, a tendency to hold forth, to inflate your role in the story, to promise as a way of feeling large in the moment. Then the gap between announcement and delivery becomes the thing people remember about you, which is bitter, because your intentions were sincere every single time. Money and commitments are where the pattern bites hardest; both tend to swing between plenty and squeeze on a cycle you eventually learn to see coming. In love you are generous and expansive, quick to celebrate a partner and slow to notice limits, and the habit worth watching is selling a future, to them and to yourself, faster than you build one. What this square is building in you, through every overreach and correction, is judgment. Not smaller dreams: better estimates. Each time you pause between the enthusiasm and the yes, size the commitment honestly, and then keep it, some of the friction converts into range. The pattern does not vanish; it matures. People who carry this aspect well end up with a rare combination, vision that still fires in middle age joined to a track record that backs it. The appetite never shrinks, and it was never supposed to. You just finally grow hands big enough to hold what it reaches for.

Sun trine Jupiter is the aspect people mean when they say someone was born under a good sign. Growth and identity cooperate in you without friction: you like who you are, you expect things to work out, and things work out often enough to keep the expectation funded. Strangers warm to you quickly. Help arrives when needed, sometimes before you ask, because your good faith in people tends to invite their best behavior. This ease produces real virtues. You are generous without keeping score, tolerant of difference, and quick to credit the honest version of someone's motives. Your outlook is wide by default; you care about meaning, fairness, and the long run, and you can lift a room simply by assuming out loud that the situation is workable. Learning tends to feel like pleasure rather than labor, and big questions, foreign places, and broad fields of knowledge draw you all your life. The shadow of a trine is never drama; it is sleep. Because fortune has been reliable, you can mistake luck for merit and comfort for completion. Effort starts to seem optional. The talent stays pleasant and shallow, opportunities get enjoyed rather than built on, and a life that could have been substantial settles for being nice. There is a subtler blindness too. People whose lives are actually hard can find your optimism glib, and your assurance that it will all work out, true enough for you, is not a law of nature. In love you are warmhearted, easy to live with, and inclined to extend the benefit of the doubt, though a partner may sometimes want more urgency from you than your contentment supplies. Being loved by you is comfortable; being fought for by you may take longer to experience. The deepening of this aspect is deliberate weight. Choose something large enough to fail at: a discipline, a cause, a standard of work that charm alone cannot meet. Practiced gratitude helps as well, since noticing your advantages is what keeps them from quietly becoming entitlements. Fortune spent on comfort evaporates; fortune invested in something beyond you compounds. Given a real task, your luck stops being a private climate and becomes what it was for all along: margin, the kind you can afford to share, and the kind that makes other people's risks possible too.

With the Sun opposite Jupiter, more tends to arrive through other people. The expansive urge is yours, but you usually meet it out there: in the friend with the grand scheme, the partner who spends what you save, the mentor whose promises outrun their delivery, the audience whose applause tempts you past your own judgment. Your life keeps staging encounters with excess, and the standing question is which side of the table it is really on. The gifts of this pair are all present in you. You are hopeful, sociable, and generous, and you genuinely enlarge through relationship: other people bring you opportunities, worldviews, and confidence you would not have generated alone. You make a natural promoter of others, seeing their possibilities at full size and saying so. That is a real service, and it wins you lasting loyalty. The push-pull shows in the swings. With some people you play the voice of reason, reining in their extravagance; with others you become the extravagant one, promising big to match an inflated picture of what they expect of you. You can alternate between the two roles for years without noticing they are one pattern seen from opposite ends. Judgment is the pressure point. Other people's enthusiasm is contagious to you, and your biggest missteps tend to be co-signed, entered on a wave of shared certainty that felt, at the time, like proof. Flattery is a particular hazard, since being seen as large is your favorite mirror, and the flatterer controls the glass. In love you are drawn to buoyant, ambitious, openhanded people. The very quality that attracts you may later read as unreliability, and whether it does often depends as much on the expectations you brought as on the partner who failed them. The maturing of this opposition is giving your confidence a home address. When your sense of scale lives inside you, checked against your actual record rather than the room's excitement, other people's enthusiasm becomes information instead of instruction. You can enjoy the big talkers without boarding every ship they launch, and encourage people without inflating them. Then the aspect pays its full dividend: a life genuinely widened by others, where the growth was mutual, the risks were chosen with open eyes, and the promises on both sides were mostly kept.

Sun conjunct Saturn welds your sense of self to your sense of duty. From early on, being someone and being responsible have felt like the same project, and you have probably never had the luxury of taking yourself lightly. There is an old streak in you: a gravity, a habit of preparing for the worst case, a suspicion of anything free. Many people with this aspect describe a childhood that asked them to grow up ahead of schedule, sometimes through circumstance, sometimes through a parent or authority figure who was distant, demanding, or absent when it mattered. The weight has a purpose, though it rarely feels that way when you are young. You build slowly and you build to last. Where others improvise, you structure; where others talk, you deliver, eventually, after checking twice. Your word means something because you price it honestly before giving it. Employers, institutions, and anyone who needs a thing actually done come to trust you in a way charm never earns. The private cost is doubt. Saturn sitting with the Sun can feel like an examiner living in your chest, grading your worth daily and rounding down. Praise slides off; criticism files itself permanently. You may hold back from visibility, or from wanting things openly, because wanting exposes you to failing in public. Joy itself can feel unearned, something to defer until the work is finished, and the work is never finished. It matters to know the trajectory of this aspect: it improves with age, reliably. The doubts are loudest in youth, when you are all standards and no record. Every decade adds evidence, and somewhere in the middle of life the authority you kept deferring to turns out to be yours. Others start seeking your judgment precisely because it was never for sale. In love you are slow, serious, and deeply constant. You show devotion through reliability rather than display, and you need a partner who can read that dialect and occasionally coax you out from behind the ledger. The lifelong task is separating worth from output. You were never only your usefulness. When some rest, some pleasure, and some love get admitted without a receipt, the discipline stops being armor and becomes what it was always becoming: quiet, durable strength that other people can lean on, and that finally includes you.

A sextile between the Sun and Saturn gives you steadiness you can draw on at will. Discipline, for you, is not a war with yourself; it is a tool within reach, picked up when needed and set down without fuss. You can plan, wait, persist, and keep your word without inner theatrics, and this quiet reliability gets noticed by exactly the people worth being noticed by. Older and more established people tend to take to you early. Something in your seriousness reads as trustworthy, and across a lifetime this brings mentors, sponsors, and responsibilities that arrive slightly ahead of your years. You handle them, which brings more. Institutions do not frighten you. You understand by instinct that rules, structures, and long timelines are instruments, and you use them while others are still resenting them. Your judgment runs conservative in the useful sense: you estimate costs honestly, expect things to take as long as they take, and rarely mistake enthusiasm for a plan. The temperament that comes with all this is even rather than heavy. You are not gloomy; you are unhurried. Frustration passes through you without doing much damage, because you never expected the world to move quickly in the first place. In love you favor loyalty over spectacle, and you are better at the long middle of a relationship than almost anyone: the years where showing up steadily is the whole art. A partner learns in time that your undemonstrative manner is not coolness but a preference for proof over performance. The limitation is the sextile's usual one: it waits to be used. Unexercised, this aspect settles into mere caution, a tidy life administered rather than led, with the patience that could have built something notable spent entirely on maintenance. What activates it is a long-range aim chosen by you rather than assigned: a craft, a body of work, a position earned across a decade. Your advantage is that once you commit, endurance costs you less than it costs others, so the compounding runs quietly in your favor. Choose the mountain and the walking takes care of itself. Over the years that adds up to the reputation this aspect quietly promises: the person whose work holds, whose word holds, and whose calm turns out to have been strength the entire time.

Sun square Saturn installs a strict examiner in your inner life. Whatever you do, some voice inside measures it against a standard just out of reach, and the grade always seems to arrive rounded down. You may have felt, from early on, that other people were allowed to simply be, while you had to qualify: through work, through correctness, through never being caught unprepared. Authority is often where the friction first showed itself. Parents, bosses, teachers, gatekeepers: encounters with them tend to leave you feeling blocked, judged, or invisible, and you can spend years either over-obeying or quietly at war, which are the same relationship worn two different ways. Obstacles seem to find your ambitions with unusual accuracy, and progress that looks easy for others arrives for you late and at full price. Here is what the difficulty is doing. A square between these two builds structure the way resistance builds muscle, and none of the effort is wasted, even when it feels wasted. Because nothing was handed to you, everything you hold, you actually hold: the skill is real, the position is earned, and the confidence, when it finally comes, is load-bearing. This is the classic signature of people who are better at fifty than anyone predicted at twenty, and it is honest to say the early decades can be lonely and grinding while the evidence accumulates. Two traps deserve naming. The first is surrender dressed as realism: deciding the examiner is right, aiming low, and calling it maturity. The second is proving as a way of life, where no achievement ever gets to count because counting was never the examiner's job. In love you may keep your wanting hidden, since wanting risks refusal. The partners who reach you are the ones patient with a slow-opening door, and your constancy repays that patience for decades. The turning point with this aspect is a question of jurisdiction. The standard is yours; the sentence is not. When you keep the high bar but fire the judge, discipline separates from self-punishment, and the same severity that once cut you becomes precision. What you build after that tends to outlast nearly everything built faster, and you come to see that the examiner, retrained, was the best teacher you had.

The Sun trine Saturn gives you composure that was never taught. Patience, realism, and follow-through sit in you as defaults rather than achievements: you keep promises without strain, respect limits without resentment, and understand in your bones that good things get built slowly. Other people work for years to acquire the steadiness you woke up with. This makes you the quiet spine of most situations you enter. At work you are the one whose estimates are honest and whose pieces are finished when the plan assumed they would be. In families and friendships you are the keeper of continuity: the one who remembers, maintains, shows up, and holds the long thread while flashier people come and go. Elders trust you early, and responsibility reaches you without the friction it costs others, because you neither chase it nor flee it. Age suits you; you tend to grow into your face, your role, and your authority on schedule. The risks here are soft-spoken, like the aspect itself. Ease with structure can become an unexamined preference for it, so you default to the proven path, the modest goal, the known devil, not from fear exactly, but from a settledness that never had a reason to question itself. You can under-dream. A life can pass, orderly and respectable, one size smaller than the person living it, and no one will ever tell you, because from the outside it looks like success. There is also a certain dryness worth watching: reliability can crowd out play, and people who love you may wish, sometimes out loud, that you would want something extravagantly for once. In love you are constant, undramatic, and slow to leave, which is mostly a blessing and occasionally an anesthetic. Steadiness should be a choice renewed, not a rut with virtues. The invitation of this trine is to spend your stability, not just bank it. Solid ground exists so something can be built on it, and you can afford risks that would capsize less balanced people. Take the larger commission, the stranger idea, the want you have been quietly deferring. Your foundations will hold; that was never in question. What the years then produce is the best version of this aspect: not merely a dependable life, but a substantial one.

Sun opposite Saturn puts the judge outside you, or so it seems. Across your life, limitation tends to wear a face: the critical parent, the withholding boss, the gatekeeper who says not yet, the partner whose sober realism lands on your plans like weather. You come to expect assessment. Walking into a room, some part of you assumes an examiner is already seated, and you either perform for them or brace against them. The real business of this opposition is that the examiner travels with you. What you meet in these people is your own standard, projected outward and then hired: you find your way, with strange consistency, to relationships and structures that test you, because something in you does not fully believe an untested self. This has costs. You can dim yourself preemptively, deferring to authority you privately outrank. Or you can live in permanent counterpunch, hearing verdicts in remarks that carried none. Relationships, especially with older or more established people, can take on a formality where respect tangles with resentment, and closeness gets deferred until you have passed whatever the current test is. Intimacy suffers when every embrace comes with a rubric attached, and the people who love you may tire of being mistaken for your judges. What this aspect gives in exchange is realism and durability that nobody can repossess. You do not confuse applause with truth. Your confidence, assembled slowly and against resistance, holds up in conditions that flatten sunnier people, and your respect, hard to earn, is worth something in a way easy approval never is. Duty and affection learn to coexist in you, and the few you finally let close discover a loyalty with actual foundations under it. The turning of the aspect comes when you bring the judge back home. The standards were yours all along; the men and women at the gate were only wearing them. When you begin grading your own work, honestly and finally, two things happen. The external critics lose their strange power over you and become merely people with opinions. And your own authority arrives, the kind this opposition was always building toward: measured, tested, earned at full price, and, from the middle of life onward, increasingly difficult for anyone to argue with.
